title: How people are using Muse
format_note: Real users on camera introduce their named AI companions; a title card and a drifting field of testimonial clips carry the proof.
one_thing: Real people name their Muse and describe what it did for them, so the product is proven by customers before any feature is shown.

transcript.voice_style: Casual first-person customer clips, one speaker per line, cut together mid-sentence; names read as a quick roll call.
transcript.script_shape: Roll call of nicknames, then a specific job (website, flights, trip), a parenting result with a number, a creator story, and a feeling line.

structure.frame0: Light white-to-blue gradient with one phone-shaped video card of a woman mid-sentence on the left and a caption pill reading 'My Muse's name is Lizzie.'; right half empty (f0001.jpg).
structure.first_3s: A person speaks, then portrait cards slide in from the edges with nickname captions (Chippy, Noodles), a cream plush mascot enters at t=2.5s (f0002.jpg, strips/window-05-2.536s.jpg).

beats.what: Customer says her Muse's name is Lizzie; nickname roll call begins.
Portraits and plush mascots with chat chips (Shopping your items, Spa day booked, Workout ready) pass by.
Hard cut back to the three-mascot composition, then a second cut to blank white.
Words of 'In the last few weeks you've had your Muse hard at work.' build in on white.
Testimonial cards drift through a blurred depth field with artifact cards, clocks, camera, map, notebook.
Last customer card grows to fill the frame with 'Here's themes for your ideas.' chip.
'And we are just getting started.' builds word by word; small print 'Muse for 18+, N. America only'.

hero_moment.what: Title card 'In the last few weeks you've had your [mascot] Muse hard at work.' lands on empty white after the cut, the only moment with no imagery.

ending.cta_text: And we are just getting started.
ending.what: Closing line completes at about 36.2s and holds about 1.6s over the age and region note; no logo or URL.

rhythm.how_change_is_paced: One 30.37 s shot (80% of runtime) from 7.47s with continuous camera drift and card swaps; change comes from cards entering and leaving, about every 2 s, not from cuts. Two cuts at 6.84s and 7.47s.

look.ground: White fading to pale blue at the bottom edge on every frame; mean luminance 0.915 at frame 0, light share 1.0.
look.accent_use: No colour accent in the type; 'Muse' picks up a blue tint only while the title is building (strips/window-08-7.407s.jpg), then turns black.
look.type: Geometric humanist sans in black, medium weight, centred; captions in a condensed white sans on a grey pill; small print in dark navy.
look.depth: Blurred far cards and sharp near cards on one plane of white; foreground cards scale up to 40-50% of frame height before leaving (f0012.jpg, f0018.jpg).

product_ui.camera_on_ui: UI cards are small chips and artifact cards beside speakers; foreground cards scale up as they approach and blur when far, with no zoom into a screen.
product_ui.notes: Chat chips like 'Your flights dropped from $350 to $270' and artifact cards 'Baby Sleeping Plan' and '20-Day Content Calendar' are readable only when near; far ones are blurred decoration (f0007.jpg, f0009.jpg). No full app screen appears; presence share is an estimate.

motion.text_entry: Title words fade in one at a time with small vertical offsets over about 1.2 s (strips/window-08-7.407s.jpg); closing line builds the same way over about 1 s (strips/window-14-35.368s.jpg).
motion.ui_motion: Chips and cards slide in from edges, swap depth from blurred to sharp, and grow as they pass the camera; artifact label cards slide up to the speaker card.
motion.camera: Constant lateral drift through a depth field, with scale-up of the nearest card; no shake.
motion.eases: Cards decelerate into place; title words ease out with a short fade. Exact curves not measured.

transitions.cause: Cut from the testimonial stream back to the three-mascot composition, then to blank white.
A new customer card enters from the edge as the previous one leaves.
A blurred background card sharpens into the next foreground card.
A chip fades in, e.g. 'Booking ticket', beside the mascot it describes.

on_screen_lines.text: In the last few weeks you've had your Muse hard at work.
And we are just getting started.

copy.holds_vs_reading_rule: Closing line holds about 1.67s for 6 words, under rule 2's 2 s floor; small print is 18 px of 720 (2.5%), under the 2.6% floor. Captions follow speech, so holds match the voice.

sound.music: Classified music at 0.74 confidence; tags percussion 0.266, keyboard_musical 0.242, synthesizer 0.213; about 99 BPM but beat confidence only 0.207. Below the 0.2 line otherwise, so no further genre named.
sound.sfx: None established from the evidence; disc_scratching tag 0.236 is not enough to claim a sound effect.
sound.vo_music_balance: Speech tag 0.716 vs music 0.659; customer speech and music share the mix. Loudness range is 1.3 LU, so the level barely moves.
sound.energy_arc: Three sections: 0-11.5s, 11.5-24.8s, 24.8-37.8s; silence span 36.9-37.8s at the end. LUFS -16.2 integrated, short-term max -15.2, true peak -5.1 dBTP.
sound.sync_to_picture: 1 of 2 cuts lands on a strong onset (share 0.5 vs chance 0.326); with two cuts that cannot show the cuts are locked to the sound.

good.observation: Real customers speaking in phone-shaped cards make the proof the picture; a name, a job and a result arrive in under 4 s of runtime each.
Burned-in captions follow speech word for word, so the film reads with sound off; every spoken line is on screen.
A blank white title card after the cut resets attention and states the premise in 11 words at 7.6% of frame height.
Depth blur separates the one sharp speaker from decoration, so a single card is the focal point in most frames.
Closing line builds word by word and stays centred and still once landed; one idea, two lines of 3 and 3 words.
The mascot chips (Shopping your items, Spa day booked, Workout ready) show jobs done as short results rather than feature names.

weak.observation: No logo, product name lockup or URL ends the film; the close is a slogan plus 2.5%-height legal text.
The right half is empty at frame 0 and several frames leave a quarter or more bare.
Product UI is shown as small blurred chips; the real app never appears, so how Muse works is not visible.
Closing title holds about 1.67 s, shorter than the 2 s last-line floor.

rule_candidates.rule: Open on one real customer speaking, with a verbatim caption, and name the product in the first sentence.
rule_candidates.evidence: f0001.jpg: 'My Muse's name is Lizzie.' at t=0

rule_candidates.rule: In a testimonial film, keep one continuous shot of 20 s or more and make change by swapping cards in a depth field instead of cutting.
rule_candidates.evidence: metrics.json longest_shot 30.37 s, 80.3% of runtime; 2 hard cuts

rule_candidates.rule: Insert one blank title card on white at 18-25% of runtime to restate the premise in at most 11 words before the proof run.
Blur background cards and keep one speaker sharp so a focal point survives a crowded field.
Caption every spoken line in a pill at 3% of frame height or more at a fixed bottom-centre position.
rule_candidates.evidence: crops/caption.png; f0001.jpg to f0018.jpg all show pill at y~585-624

rule_candidates.rule: Build a closing line word by word, then hold it at least 2 s; this film holds about 1.67 s for 6 words.
Small print stays at 2.6% of the short side or more; this film's 18 px (2.5%) is the weakest legible element.
Music at -16.2 LUFS with true peak -5.1 dBTP falls 2.2 LU under the social target; master testimonial films at -14 LUFS.

unchecked: Title hold times before 36 s: sample interval 2 s hides when the 8.7 s title leaves.
